_doc: PHASE 2 PRE-REGISTRATION -- written BEFORE any remap netlist, liberty, deck or verification script of this run existed. Phase 2 of the pass-gate (transmission-gate) cell study: remap qal/synth/threeway/sha_slice.v onto the TG-XOR/TG-MUX cells characterised in Phase 1 (qal/pgcell/RESULTS.json) plus shallow-stack statics, and price it. Own directory qal/pgcell/p2/. NOTHING is written to qal/sha256/ (the sibling NAND2-only run) -- it is read-only input here.

inherited_phase1_facts_MEASURED.phase1_verdict: the alternating chain does NOT hold; pass-gate stages compound with the bank's own non-restoration faster than one inverter-class stage repairs

acceptance_gates.G0_ANCHOR: Independently re-extract the COMMITTED netlist census (cell count, type histogram, device count, total device width, logic depth, per-level profile) from qal/synth/threeway/work/sha_slice.cmos.v and the PDK spice, with code written for this run. PASS = cell count and type histogram reproduce the committed 56-cell census exactly. The DEPTH is reported as measured, whatever it is; the brief's 'depth 10' is treated as a CLAIM TO BE CHECKED, not a given.
acceptance_gates.E1_SAT_MITER: yosys: miter -equiv -flatten -make_assert gold gate; sat -verify -prove-asserts. PASS = 'SAT proof finished - no model found: SUCCESS!' Required for EVERY remap variant reported.
acceptance_gates.E2_EQUIV_INDUCT: yosys equiv_make / equiv_simple / equiv_induct / equiv_status -assert. A structurally different engine. PASS = 'Equivalence successfully proven'.
acceptance_gates.E5_PORTS: gate module port list and widths identical to the RTL, read back from yosys write_json (not a regex).
acceptance_gates.E3_VECTORS: >= 151,584 vectors, 0 mismatches -- the standard the committed QDI form met. Adopting the sibling qal/sha256/verify.py vector construction (all 65,536 (a,b) pairs exhaustive so the 8-bit CPA is COMPLETE, + 64 per-bit exhaustive maj/ch covers, + pseudo-random to carry the total past 151,584).
acceptance_gates.C_COST: Report for every variant: cell count, transistor (device) count, total device width, logic depth, per-level cell profile. Against BOTH the committed netlist AND a NAND2-only mapping.
acceptance_gates.D_RESTORATION: Derive the restoration rule from Phase 1's MEASURED per-bank chain data (not from theory), apply it to the remap, and report what it costs in cells / devices / depth.

declared_method.route_A: STRUCTURAL hand remap exploiting the identity maj(a,b,c) = (a^b) ? c : a and c_out = (a^b) ? c_in : a -- i.e. the carry and majority functions ARE 2:1 muxes, which is exactly what a transmission gate is natively. Proven by SAT, not by assertion.
declared_method.route_B: ABC liberty-constrained mapping onto the same restricted cell set, as an INDEPENDENT cross-check that the hand remap is not worse than what a mapper finds.
declared_method.route_N: my own NAND2-only (inv+nand2) mapping, to cross-check the sibling run's NAND2-only numbers rather than quoting them unchecked.
declared_method.AOI_OAI_decomposition: TO BE REPORTED AS FOUND. The committed netlist's 14 AOI/OAI cells (6 a21oi + 5 o21ai + 3 a21o) are carry-chain and majority cells; the declared hypothesis is that they are ABSORBED into TG muxes rather than decomposed into NAND2 trees. If that hypothesis fails, the NAND2/INV decomposition actually used will be reported instead.

PRE_STATED_PREDICTIONS_to_be_scored.P1_cells: The pass-gate remap will use FEWER cells than the committed 56, and far fewer than a NAND2-only mapping. Stated bound: <= 45 cells.
PRE_STATED_PREDICTIONS_to_be_scored.P2_devices: Device count will be BELOW the committed netlist's, because TG-XNOR2 (8 dev) < static xnor2 (10 dev) and TG-MUX2 (6 dev) < static mux2 (12 dev). Stated bound: <= 300 devices vs the committed count.
PRE_STATED_PREDICTIONS_to_be_scored.P3_depth: Logic DEPTH will be WORSE (larger) than the committed netlist's, because the mux carry chain is a ripple and each carry stage is its own cell. Stated direction: PG depth > committed depth.
PRE_STATED_PREDICTIONS_to_be_scored.P4_restoration_cost: Applying the measured restoration rule will roughly DOUBLE the cell count of the pass-gate remap and will erase most of the device-count advantage. Stated bound: restored variant device count within +-25% of the committed netlist's.
PRE_STATED_PREDICTIONS_to_be_scored.P5_verdict: The pass-gate remap will PASS formal equivalence and vectors (it is a Boolean identity), and will FAIL the electrical admission rule inherited from Phase 1, because the carry chain wants more consecutive pass-gate levels than the measured budget allows.

declared_limitations_stated_in_advance: Phase 2 is a STRUCTURAL and FORMAL exercise. The vector check and the SAT proof validate the BOOLEAN remap only -- they run on behavioural cell models and say NOTHING about level loss, settling or rail draw. The electrical verdict is Phase 1's and is inherited, not re-measured here.

Device counts and total device widths are MEASURED from the PDK spice netlists (for statics) and from the Phase 1 emitted TG netlists. Any ENERGY figure derived from them is DERIVED, and any figure resting on the campaign's committed per-gate energy is a BOOKING carried forward from that source.
No new SPICE deck is required by this phase's deliverable. If any is run it will be declared and its numbers labelled MEASURED separately.

The sibling run qal/sha256/ is read-only input. Its NAND2-only numbers are quoted as ITS measurement and are additionally cross-checked by my own independent mapping; where the two disagree, both are reported.
